highlights.why_it_matters: The most painful Rust tradeoff — first build takes 45 seconds. This is the real DX cost of Rust's compile-time guarantees.

highlights.label: Startup time — 89ms
highlights.why_it_matters: Native binary — zero JIT, zero warmup. Ready to serve 11k RPS from the first request.

highlights.label: Memory at idle — 8.2 MB RSS
highlights.why_it_matters: Rust's zero-cost abstractions deliver: 8 MB to run a production-ready microservice with DB pool.

highlights.label: Memory under load — 36.7 MB (c=200)
highlights.why_it_matters: 2x Rust memory under load. Reasonable trade-off for 2.55x better throughput.

highlights.label: Startup time — 288ms (3.2x slower than Rust/Go)
highlights.why_it_matters: JIT compilation adds a fixed 200ms warmup tax. Fine for long-running services, painful for cold starts / serverless.

highlights.label: Latency spike at c=200 — avg 47ms, max 956ms
highlights.output:
Thread Stats   Avg      Stdev     Max   +/- Stdev
    Latency    47.37ms   96.92ms 934.01ms   90.37%
    Req/Sec     1.85k   293.47     2.64k    66.91%
  Requests/sec:  14427.40
highlights.why_it_matters: The 96ms stdev reveals GC pause spikes. The 934ms max means some requests waited nearly a second — unacceptable for p99 SLAs.

highlights.label: Memory explosion — 357 MB under load
highlights.why_it_matters: 20x more memory than Rust under the same load. At 100 microservice instances, that's 35 GB vs 1.7 GB.

highlights.label: Strong write throughput — 8,632 RPS POST
highlights.why_it_matters: Write-heavy workloads are where dotnet holds its own — within 1% of Rust for DB inserts.
